chapters.title: In the Presence of Danger
chapters.sourcePressure: A real present cue deserves more authority than the social pressure to seem agreeable; Kelly carrying groceries upstairs is the frozen source case for how insistence after refusal can turn politeness into danger.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a refused boundary being pressed again as information and move before social proof catches up.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing fear to general anxiety or teaching readers to be suspicious of everyone.

chapters.title: The Technology of Intuition
chapters.sourcePressure: Intuition is presented as a practical process of fast cue recognition, useful only when tied back to concrete perception rather than treated as magic.
chapters.coreMove: Translate a gut signal into the cue that produced it before deciding what to do.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating intuition as mystical certainty or as always correct.

chapters.title: The Academy of Prediction
chapters.sourcePressure: Prediction means disciplined pattern reading: repeated behavior, sequence, and earlier action matter more than excuse-making or absolute certainty.
chapters.coreMove: Build a forecast from repeated behavior and sequence, then choose the narrowest protective action it justifies.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning prediction into prophecy or claiming impossible accuracy.

chapters.title: Survival Signals
chapters.sourcePressure: Survival signals are early warning cues whose meaning comes from clustering and context, not from a single odd detail isolated from the scene.
chapters.coreMove: Cluster small signals in context before deciding whether the pattern deserves action.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating every odd cue as proof of danger.

chapters.title: Imperfect Strangers
chapters.sourcePressure: The stranger label is weak; official site guidance moves attention from category to behavior, context, access, and pressure.
chapters.coreMove: Shift the safety question from who this person is to what this person is doing right now.
chapters.commonMisread: Teaching naive trust or saying stranger status never matters.

chapters.title: High-stakes predictions
chapters.sourcePressure: Consequential risk assessment requires stronger pattern support, but high stakes can justify earlier protective action before certainty is available.
chapters.coreMove: Match the size of your action to the strength of the pattern and the cost of being late.
chapters.commonMisread: Claiming uncertainty disappears before action is justified.

chapters.title: Promises to kill (understanding threats)
chapters.sourcePressure: Threats are data to interpret by function, context, and sequence; words alone are weaker than words embedded in a behavioral pattern.
chapters.coreMove: Read a threat by what it is trying to accomplish and what behavior surrounds it.
chapters.commonMisread: Either dismissing threats as talk or treating any ugly sentence as certain violence.

chapters.title: Persistence, persistence (dealing with people who refuse to let go)
chapters.sourcePressure: Repeated pursuit after refusal is meaningful data; ambiguity and ongoing negotiation can feed a pattern that clear refusal and reduced access interrupt.
chapters.coreMove: Stop rewarding pursuit with negotiation once refusal has already been given.
chapters.commonMisread: Romanticizing persistence as sincerity or treating all repeated contact as identical danger.

chapters.title: Occupational hazards (violence in the workplace)
chapters.sourcePressure: Workplaces can normalize grievance, access conflict, and escalation through routine process; institutions need processes that preserve behavioral signal instead of burying it.
chapters.coreMove: Make workplace process capture repeated grievance and access pressure before one decisive incident appears.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating workplace violence as a sudden HR surprise or reducing it to disgruntlement.

chapters.title: Intimate enemies (domestic violence)
chapters.sourcePressure: Intimacy can distort warning interpretation; control, recurrence, and escalation still matter even when apology, reconciliation, or outside stories soften the read.
chapters.coreMove: Give repeated control behavior more weight than apology or closeness when safety is at stake.
chapters.commonMisread: Offering one-size domestic-violence doctrine or victim-blaming readers for complex constraints.

chapters.title: "I was trying to let him down easy" (date stalking)
chapters.sourcePressure: Politeness, gentle rejection, and minimization can be exploited as false access; persistence after refusal matters more than sincerity framing.
chapters.coreMove: Make refusal unmistakable and close the access loop when persistence starts feeding on ambiguity.
chapters.commonMisread: Teaching cruelty, blame, or legal doctrine instead of behavioral clarity.

chapters.title: Fear of children (violent children)
chapters.sourcePressure: Innocence assumptions can delay intervention; repeated signals, access, fixation, and escalation still deserve behavior-first attention in youth danger.
chapters.coreMove: Name repeated youth warning signals early enough for intervention, without hiding behind innocence.
chapters.commonMisread: Diagnosing children or implying every troubled child is violent.

chapters.title: Better to be wanted by the police than not to be wanted at all (attacks against public figures)
chapters.sourcePressure: Visibility, recognition motives, grievance, repeated approach behavior, and access can shape attacks against public figures; theatricality does not make a pattern harmless.
chapters.coreMove: Treat public-facing threat behavior as a pattern of recognition, grievance, and access seeking, not as mere drama.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating public-figure attacks as celebrity trivia or agency doctrine.

chapters.title: Extreme hazards
chapters.sourcePressure: Some severe hazards offer thin predictive signal; when clean prediction is weak, preparation, margin, and humility matter more than overconfident forecasting.
chapters.coreMove: When signal is thin, stop pretending to know and build margin for the hazard instead.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning rare hazards into panic or catastrophic statistics.

chapters.title: The gift of fear
chapters.sourcePressure: The close integrates signal, intuition, boundary clarity, preparation, and the distinction between evidence-bound fear and worry or panic.
chapters.coreMove: Keep fear useful by checking whether it is attached to present evidence, then let it guide boundaries and action.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating every anxious feeling as truth or turning fear into a philosophy.
